page.title: What Is Virtual Event Production
page.description: Learn what virtual event production covers, how it differs from platform licences, typical costs, timelines, staffing and the deliverables you should expect.
page.definition: Virtual event production is the end-to-end service that designs, rehearses and runs a live online experience, covering run of show, speaker preparation, branded assets, live switching, backup streams and post-event recordings.
page.quick_answer: Treat production as a separate purchase from the platform; budget two thousand five hundred to seven thousand five hundred for a moderated webinar and ten thousand to fifty thousand plus for a summit, then lock the platform and venue AV six to eight weeks out.

sections.h2: What does virtual event production include?

blocks.p: Production delivers the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream that turn a platform licence into a reliable live show.

ul: Run of show with cue points and contingency triggers
Speaker brief and rehearsal on the real platform
Branded slide template and lower thirds
Edited recording and short clips delivered within twenty-four to forty-eight hours

sections.h2: How much does virtual event production cost?

sections.h2: What is the difference between platform and production?

blocks.p: The platform is software; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream, and West Peek Productions does not sell event software but produces events on the platform you choose.

ul: Platform licence gives you the streaming room and registration tools
Production provides the show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator
One producer can run a simple webinar; summits and hybrid events need a full crew
Lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final

sections.h2: What timeline and staffing do you need?

blocks.p: Lead time is six to eight weeks for a summit or conference and three to four weeks for a webinar, with staffing scaling to match complexity.

ol: Week one to two: intake, brief and platform selection
Week three to four: speaker briefs, branded assets and rehearsal scheduling
Week five to six: full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before live
Live day: technical check sixty minutes before go live
Post-event: replay and clips delivered within twenty-four to forty-eight hours

sections.h2: How do you plan and run a virtual event?

blocks.p: Seven stages each have one owner and one output, moving from intake through reporting with approval gates at each step.

ul: Intake: scope, goals and platform confirmed
Brief: run of show, speaker list and asset list locked
Production: rehearsals, lower thirds built, backup stream tested
Review: internal dry run with all speakers
Approval: sign-off on final run of show
Publishing: live event executed with moderation
Reporting: attendance, engagement and lead data delivered

faq.q: Can I use my existing Zoom Webinars or Microsoft Teams licence?
faq.a: Yes, production works on the platform you already use such as Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24 or StreamYard, and the crew adapts to its features and limits.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book production for a hybrid conference?
faq.a: Plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks out; lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final to avoid last-minute gaps.

faq.q: What tools does the production team use for planning and follow-up?
faq.a: Typical tools include Zoom Events, Cvent or Bizzabo for the event; Eventbrite or Cvent for registration; Asana or Monday.com for the plan; HubSpot or Salesforce for follow-up.

faq.q: Does West Peek Productions sell the streaming platform?
faq.a: West Peek Productions does not sell event software; it produces events on the platform you choose and can help you choose it.
